requirements.description: The system must allow visitors and customers to enter the virtual store and browse the main catalog.
The system must organize products by animal categories, including fish, dogs, reptiles, cats and birds.
The system must allow access to categories through different navigation paths, such as the main menu, quick shortcuts and visual elements on the home page.
The system must allow viewing the list of products for each category.
The system must allow viewing of available items for each product.
The system must allow viewing of the details of each item, including description, identification, price and stock status.
The system must allow searching for products by keyword.
The search must consider the product name as the basis for returning results.
When no keyword is entered, the system must prevent the search and guide the user to fill in the search field.
The system must allow the registration of new customers by filling in identification, contact, address and access credentials.
The system must allow the client to authenticate by providing username and password.
The system must inform you when authentication cannot be completed due to an invalid username or password.
The system must allow the customer to end their usage session.
The system must allow the customer to edit their registration data and profile preferences.
The system must allow the customer to define their preferred language.
The system must allow the customer to choose a favorite category.
The system should allow the customer to enable a personalized list of products based on their favorite category.
The system must allow the customer to enable the display of a promotional banner related to their favorite category.
The system must allow adding items to the shopping cart from the product and item detail pages.
When the same item is added more than once, the system must consolidate the item in the cart and increase its quantity.
The system must allow viewing the cart with a list of selected items, quantities, unit prices and totals per item.
The system must inform, for each item in the cart, whether it is available in stock at the time of inclusion.
The system must allow updating the quantities of items in the cart.
The system must allow removing items from the cart.
When the quantity entered for an item is less than 1, the system must remove it from the cart.
The system should automatically calculate the cart subtotal based on the selected items and quantities.
The system must inform stock availability when viewing the item.
When there is no quantity available in stock, the system must indicate that the item is on order.
When completing an order, the system must record the write-off of the quantity purchased from stock.
The system must require the user to be authenticated to begin the purchase closing process.
When starting an order, the system must use the customer's registration data to initially fill in the billing and delivery information.
The system must use the items in the cart to automatically compose the order.
The system must allow the customer to enter or adjust the order's payment details.
The system must allow choosing the type of card from the options provided by the application.
The system must allow the customer to indicate a delivery address different from the billing address.
When the customer chooses a different delivery address, the system must present a specific step to fill in that address.
Before completion, the system must present a confirmation step with the billing and delivery data entered.
The system should complete the order only after explicit confirmation from the customer.
When completing the order, the system must generate a unique identifier for the purchase.
When completing the order, the system must record the purchase date, the items purchased, the quantities, values ​​and the initial status of the order.
After completing the purchase, the system must clear the customer's cart.
After completing the purchase, the system should display a message confirming receipt of the order.
The system must allow the customer to consult the list of orders already placed.
The system must present, in the order list, at least the order number, the date and the total value.
The system must allow consultation of the details of a specific order.
When detailing the order, the system must present payment data, addresses, carrier, status, purchased items, quantities, prices and total purchase value.
The system must restrict the viewing of orders to the respective customer responsible for the purchase.
The system must protect the purchase closing and order query functionalities through customer authentication.
The system must properly terminate the client session during the logout process, avoiding undue continuity of authenticated access.
The system should not unnecessarily expose the customer's password during navigation after login.
The system must maintain consistency between cart, order and stock, avoiding discrepancies between the purchase made and the registered items.
The system must ensure that the order is recorded with all its main elements, including header, status and purchased items.
The system must guarantee unique order numbering, allowing traceability of purchases.
The system must automatically calculate cart and order values, reducing the risk of manual error.
The system must handle invalid entries in a controlled manner, displaying appropriate messages to the user without compromising the continuity of the application.
The system must prevent inconsistent operations, such as starting a purchase without authentication or trying to manipulate non-existent items silently.
The system must preserve the order history for later consultation by the customer.
The system must offer simple and understandable navigation, with clear access to categories, search, cart, customer account and help.
The purchasing process must be conducted in logical and progressive steps, facilitating customer understanding during checkout.
The system must provide guidance and confirmation messages at important points in the flow, such as login failure, empty search field and completed order.
The system must consult the stock situation in an up-to-date manner at critical points in the purchasing journey.
The system must reflect the preferences registered by the customer, such as a personalized list and banner associated with the favorite category.
